blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) fall under Part IV, Articles 36–51, and are non-justiciable.
DPSP is divided into three distinct categories.
Fundamental Duties are enshrined in Article 51A and comprise 11 duties.
Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment in 1976 and modified by the 86th Amendment in 2002.
Constitutional Amendments are carried out under Article 368.
DPSPs (Articles 36–51) are non-justiciable in a court of law.
Article 51A contains Fundamental Duties, introduced by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
The 86th Amendment (2002) extended the Fundamental Duties.
Article 368 provides the power and process for amending the Constitution.
